text: An important update found while researching this lesson: Chainlink's own docs currently show both Automation and Functions as deprecated, with guidance to migrate to the Chainlink Runtime Environment.
Checked live against the current docs, not assumed — this course is being built after both deprecation dates already passed.
Automation solved a specific gap: a contract can't wake itself up. checkUpkeep is simulated off-chain at no cost; performUpkeep only executes when true, and re-checks its own condition before acting.

Functions solved a different gap: computation or an authenticated API call the contract can't make itself. A decentralized oracle network executes submitted code independently and aggregates the results.

Both problems don't go away just because the products did: something has to trigger logic without a human, and something has to bridge off-chain computation in safely. CRE is Chainlink's current answer.
Next up, Lesson 20 builds something smaller and very current: a backend service that watches a Chainlink price feed and triggers an action when it crosses a threshold.
